stops.note: 'pursued man, outlaw', from tóir 'pursuit'; applied to Irish Catholics dispossessed in the Cromwellian conquest who took to banditry
in the Exclusion Crisis of 1679-81, opponents mocked supporters of the Catholic James, Duke of York, as 'Tories', Irish bandits; the name stuck to Britain's Conservatives

current_meaning: a member or supporter of the British Conservative Party
